existingCodeObservations.finding: Overlay running state comes from session.IsRunning while active selection is calculated separately from the controller's active session.
Running swaps the hover action between pause and resume; active sets a border that is hidden for IsNavigator; nonactive overlays use the configured opacity; clock mode disables pausing.

implementationConstraints: These are proposed visual state cues, not existing implemented state badges. Do not change timer/session behavior as part of this design exploration.
Active selection must stay visible when paused and must not be inferred from the running flag.

For selected option 5 revision 2, show the ACTIVE tab only for the selected timer and retain the running/pause marker beside the project name. Do not render a project-name underline or import option 1's separate running/paused text pills.
Use shape or text alongside color so running, paused and active are distinguishable without relying only on color.
Reserve stable space for status cues; toggling state must not reflow or resize the timer or obscure live text and artwork.
State indicators are noninteractive. The running triangle is a status symbol; the hover control separately shows the action the user can take: Pause while running, Resume while paused.
No new blinking or continuous animation is proposed. Keep time and project text readable in all states.

The comparison uses equal opacity to isolate state cues. Existing user-configured nonactive-overlay opacity remains independent and will be addressed in the next layer; pausing alone must not imply nonactive opacity.
Real-time clock mode must not receive a misleading paused cue; mode-specific labels and disabled pause presentation remain to be resolved before implementation.
The inactive/reset zero state is distinct from a paused session if the session model exposes that distinction; this board compares only running and paused examples.

backgroundOpacity.renderingNote: AI-generated concept preview of opacity differences, not measured alpha compositing. Exact blending and readability over real desktop content remain to be checked in the implemented overlay.

unselectedTimerOpacity.userWording: 40% is better. what is next step?
unselectedTimerOpacity.compositionRule: Overall unselected opacity multiplies the existing per-layer opacity: effective background alpha = 0.70 * overall opacity. Percentages describe the intended setting; the generated image is an illustrative preview, not measured alpha compositing.
unselectedTimerOpacity.selectionRule: Only selection controls this dimming. An unselected timer may still be running, and a selected paused timer remains at full overall opacity.
unselectedTimerOpacity.activeTabRule: Show the ACTIVE tab on selected timers only; unselected timers have no tab or underline.
unselectedTimerOpacity.hoverToolbarOpacityPolicy: The approved settings design applies keep-opaque behavior before unselected dimming, including hover controls. The dimming comparison itself does not show an unselected hover toolbar; verify popup opacity explicitly during implementation.

existingCodeObservations.finding: BackgroundOpacity is normalized to 0-100 and its code default is 50. InactiveSeparatedOverlayOpacity has a code default of 35. These are code defaults, not a live reading of the user's settings or newly selected design defaults.

The existing appearance model combines a shared background opacity with per-part opaque flags. Numeric per-layer sliders and state-indicator opacity mapping have not been selected or implemented in this design session.

The current host has a left live preview, middle navigation and right scrolling inspector, with a 1060x740 initial size and 840x600 minimum. Background opacity uses 0-100; the unselected-opacity slider uses 10-100. Existing detail checkboxes force named parts opaque.
Selectors, sliders and checkboxes call CommitControls as they change; DoneButton_Click closes the window. The proposed panel keeps this immediate-apply interaction model.

constraints: Keep running/paused state independent from active selection and from opacity.

The background-opacity board varies only background/map opacity. The unselected-timer board fixes the background setting at 70% and varies overall opacity for unselected clocks, including their frame and text.
Do not silently apply a new opacity default or alter user settings based on the concept images.

Nonactive-overlay dimming remains separate from background opacity. Settings previews show selected and unselected sample timers; preview-only state/backdrop controls must never start, pause or select real timers.
Use the approved project-name running/pause marker and top-center ACTIVE tab; never restore the removed underline.
